dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A family of interpolation-problem types indexed by a natural number n. The supplied constructor and projections show that an element carries n+1 real nodes, n+1 real data values, a real evaluation point, and a proof that the node map is injective.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the universally quantified problem object and builds pairwise distinctness of the nodes into the domain of the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second projection of a problem, namely its data vector f : Fin (n+1) → Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the values to which the interpolation functional, perturbation model, and condition expression are applied.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real vectors ell and f of length n, it is the ratio (Σ_i |ell_i f_i|)/|Σ_i ell_i f_i|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the Lagrange weights and problem data, it is the asserted limiting condition number and the quantity asserted to be at least 1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: It asserts that the function epsilon ↦ LocalDef012 ell f epsilon tends to the stated condition as epsilon tends to 0 through strictly positive real values.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the first conjunct: a right-hand limit of the worst-case normalized relative output change.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: It constructs the vector of Lagrange basis values at the problem's evaluation point from the problem's nodes.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These values are the coefficients ell used in the computed interpolation value, condition expression, and perturbation response.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The scalar Σ_j ell_j f_j, where ell is the Lagrange-weight vector and f is the problem data.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The sole explicit hypothesis is that this computed interpolation value is nonzero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: A constructor packaging nodes : Fin (n+1) → Real, data : Fin (n+1) → Real, an evaluation point x : Real, and a proof that the node map is injective into a LocalDef001 n value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It shows that every quantified problem includes pairwise distinct nodes; the injectivity proof does not otherwise enter the numerical expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first projection of a problem, namely its node vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the nodes used to construct the Lagrange weights.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The third projection of a problem, namely its real evaluation point.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the point at which all Lagrange basis values are evaluated.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: The linear functional L_ell(f) = Σ_i ell_i f_i over all finite indices.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the computed value and both the original and perturbed scalar outputs.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For nodes t, evaluation point x, and index j, it is ell_j = (∏_{k≠j}(x-t_k))/(∏_{k≠j}(t_j-t_k)), with omitted or empty product factors represented by 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the standard Lagrange interpolation coefficient at x for each of the n+1 pairwise distinct nodes.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: For epsilon, it is the real supremum of the set of normalized relative output changes generated by all admissible perturbation vectors.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the worst-case response function whose positive-side limit at zero is asserted.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The set of real q for which there exists a perturbation deltaF satisfying the componentwise bound and q = LocalDef015(ell,f,deltaF)/epsilon.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each member of the supremum depend existentially on a perturbation admissible for that epsilon.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: The admissibility condition ∀j, |deltaF_j| ≤ epsilon |f_j|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It imposes componentwise relative perturbation bounds; if f_j=0 and epsilon is positive, that component cannot be perturbed.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: The relative scalar-output change |L_ell(f)-L_ell(f+deltaF)|/|L_ell(f)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: After an additional division by epsilon, it is the quantity maximized by the supremum.

binders: For every natural number n, including n=0.
For every problem carrying nodes t : Fin (n+1) → Real, data f : Fin (n+1) → Real, an evaluation point x : Real, and a proof that t is injective.
Under a proof of the hypothesis that the computed scalar interpolation value is nonzero.
hypotheses: The node map is injective as part of the problem object, so t_j ≠ t_k whenever j ≠ k.
With ell_j the Lagrange coefficient at x and v = Σ_j ell_j f_j, assume v ≠ 0.
conclusions: The supremal normalized relative output change W(epsilon) converges to κ = (Σ_j |ell_j f_j|)/|v| as epsilon tends to 0 through positive real values.
The same quantity κ satisfies 1 ≤ κ.
mathematical_definitions: Let I = Fin (n+1), the index set with n+1 elements.
For each j in I, define ell_j = (∏_{k in I, k≠j}(x-t_k))/(∏_{k in I, k≠j}(t_j-t_k)); empty products are 1.
For any real vector g indexed by I, define L_ell(g) = Σ_{j in I} ell_j g_j.
Define the computed value v = L_ell(f) and κ = (Σ_{j in I} |ell_j f_j|)/|v|.
For real epsilon, a perturbation deltaF : I → Real is admissible when |deltaF_j| ≤ epsilon |f_j| for every j.
For an admissible deltaF, define its relative output change R(deltaF) = |L_ell(f)-L_ell(f+deltaF)|/|L_ell(f)|, where addition is pointwise.
Define S_epsilon = {q in Real | there exists deltaF such that deltaF is admissible and q = R(deltaF)/epsilon}.
Define W(epsilon) = sSup(S_epsilon), using Lean's real supremum convention, which returns the supremum for a nonempty bounded-above set and 0 otherwise.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite interpolation problem with n+1 pairwise distinct real nodes, arbitrary real data, and an arbitrary real evaluation point, let ell be the vector of Lagrange basis values at that point and suppose the resulting interpolated scalar v = Σ_j ell_j f_j is nonzero. Under componentwise relative data perturbations satisfying |deltaF_j| ≤ epsilon |f_j|, take the supremum of the relative change in v divided by epsilon. As epsilon approaches zero through positive values, this worst-case normalized change converges to (Σ_j |ell_j f_j|)/|v|, and that limiting condition quantity is at least 1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The implication makes no assertion for problems whose computed value v is zero; those cases are excluded by the explicit hypothesis.
The theorem allows every natural n, including n=0, so the one-node case is included.
Repeated nodes are excluded because injectivity is stored in the problem object.
The evaluation point x is unrestricted; it need not differ from the nodes or lie in their convex hull.
Individual data values need not be nonzero. For positive epsilon, a zero data component forces its corresponding perturbation component to be zero.
The perturbation model is specifically componentwise relative: it is not an arbitrary normwise perturbation model.
The output error is a relative scalar error measured with real absolute value, and the denominator is protected only by the assumption v≠0.
The limit samples only epsilon>0. No direct condition on negative epsilon is relevant to the stated convergence.
The supremum is totalized to 0 for an empty or unbounded set, although the proposition does not separately state nonemptiness or boundedness of S_epsilon.

The proposition encodes exact real arithmetic only. It contains no floating-point rounding model, implementation algorithm, error accumulation, finite precision, rate of convergence, or claim that the supremum is attained.
